column1: Why does a fixed footer need bottom space reserved in the page shell?
column2: Fixed-position elements are removed from normal document flow, so the page needs matching bottom padding to prevent its last content from being hidden underneath the footer.

column1: How are full-viewport authenticated pages sized with the fixed navbar?
column2: Their viewport height uses `100dvh - 2.5rem`, matching the footer's `h-10` height, so the screen content ends above the navbar.

column1: Where is the authenticated fixed navbar shell implemented?
column2: In `store/UserStoreProvider.tsx`, which wraps authenticated children with a reserved main region and fixed footer navigation.

column1: Where does onboarding refresh the in-memory user after saving?
column2: In `features/onboarding/hooks/useOnboardingHook.ts`, through `refetchUserAndSaveToUserStore`.

column1: Why must onboarding await the database update before refetching the user?
column2: The refetch must happen after persistence completes; otherwise it can read and store the pre-update user record.

column1: How is the refetched onboarding user synchronized with Zustand?
column2: The hook calls `getCurrentUser` and passes the result, or `null` when absent, to the store's `useUser` setter.

column1: Which routes are publicly reachable for Google OAuth review?
column2: `/login`, `/privacy-policy`, and `/terms-of-service` are allowed by the `PUBLIC_ROUTES` set in `middleware.ts`; other unauthenticated routes redirect to `/login`.

column1: Where are the public legal pages implemented?
column2: `app/privacy-policy/page.tsx` and `app/terms-of-service/page.tsx` define the content, while `features/legal/components/LegalDocument.tsx` provides their shared server-rendered layout.

column1: What Google account information does the current privacy policy describe?
column2: The verified Google profile's `name` and `email` are used to create or find the El-Bus Fen user. The Google credential is verified but not stored, and the current user profile does not store the Google photo or account identifier.

column1: What session cookie does El-Bus Fen create after Google sign-in?
column2: It creates an encrypted, HTTP-only `auth-token` cookie with a seven-day lifetime so the app can recognize the authenticated user without storing the Google password or credential.

column1: What data does the BusEntry model preserve?
column2: It stores the submitting `userId`, selected bus `time`, stable `busStop` ID, optional `busRoute`, latitude, longitude, and automatic `createdAt`/`updatedAt` timestamps.

column1: Why does a bus entry store both `time` and `createdAt`?
column2: `time` represents the selected bus event time, while `createdAt` records when the user actually submitted the log.

column1: Which repository method returns bounded recent bus entries?
column2: `getRecentBusEntries` sorts by `createdAt` descending and clamps the requested limit between 1 and 1000 to avoid unbounded log reads.

column1: What indexes support recent BusEntry queries?
column2: Compound indexes cover `{ busStop, createdAt }`, `{ busRoute, createdAt }`, and `{ userId, createdAt }`, with newest entries ordered first.

column1: What Mongoose 9 filter type does the bus-entry repository use?
column2: It uses the named `QueryFilter` type; the older `FilterQuery` export is not available as a usable generic in this project's installed Mongoose typings.

column1: How does `getLastSevenHoursBusEntries` define recent entries?
column2: It filters entries where `createdAt` is greater than or equal to seven hours before the current instant, then sorts them newest first.

column1: Why does the seven-hour query not manually add UTC+3?
column2: A rolling duration uses absolute JavaScript `Date` values, so `Date.now() - seven hours` is timezone-independent. UTC+3 only matters when calculating local calendar boundaries.

column1: What user data is returned by the seven-hour bus-entry query?
column2: It populates the `userId` reference and excludes `passwordHash` from the populated User document.

column1: Why does `Map.tsx` need to parse `entry.time` before calling date methods?
column2: The repository serializes database results across the server-client boundary, converting `Date` values into ISO strings. The map must reconstruct a `Date` before using `getHours()` or `getMinutes()`.

column1: What happens when a bus entry has an invalid timestamp?
column2: The map logs the invalid entry and skips it, preventing one malformed record from crashing the whole map effect.

column1: Where is the selected bus time converted using `UTC_OFFSET`?
column2: Inside the server-side `addBusEntry` flow in `features/shared/repositories/bus-entry-repo.ts`, keeping the environment variable out of client code.

column1: How is a selected 12-hour bus time stored?
column2: The repository converts hour/AM-PM to 24-hour time, builds today's local date using the configured offset, subtracts that offset, and stores the resulting UTC `Date`.

column1: What does `UTC_OFFSET=3` mean for a selected 7:14 AM entry?
column2: The stored instant is `04:14Z`; the user selected 7:14 in the UTC+3 local clock, and the database stores the equivalent UTC instant.

column1: Why was `StopsSelector` removed from onboarding?
column2: Routes and stops have different data shapes, so `FirstPage` now renders separate selectors tailored to each entity.

column1: What values do the onboarding selectors store?
column2: The route selector stores `route.name_en`, while the stop selector stores the stable `stop.id`.

column1: How does the map restrict entries to the current user?
column2: It filters persisted entries and realtime markers by matching `busRoute` with the authenticated user's selected route.

column1: Why does the transient map marker include `busRoute`?
column2: Realtime socket clients need the route on each marker to reject entries belonging to other bus routes before rendering them.

column1: How does the map recenter when a bus stop is selected?
column2: `features/map/components/RecenterMap.tsx` uses React Leaflet's `useMap()` hook and calls Leaflet `flyTo` with the selected stop coordinates while preserving the current zoom.

column1: Why does the map use `flyTo` instead of changing `MapContainer.center`?
column2: `MapContainer.center` initializes the map but does not reliably update an existing instance. `flyTo` responds to later selection changes and animates the movement without remounting the map.

column1: What is the gotcha with `RecenterMap`?
column2: It must render inside `MapContainer` so React Leaflet's map context is available; forcing a `MapContainer` remount would reset zoom and interaction state.

column1: Where does the bus-entry submitting state live?
column2: In `features/map/useMapHook.ts`, which sets `isSubmitting` around the awaited persistence call and exposes it to the form through the hook API.

column1: When does bus-entry submission show a success toast?
column2: Only after `addBusEntry` returns a saved entry; the success toast is emitted with Sonner after the database operation succeeds.

column1: Why is the toast host mounted in the root layout?
column2: A single root-level Sonner host lets any client feature call `toast.success` while keeping the notification portal available across routes.

column1: How are normal map entry tooltips made visually custom?
column2: Their Leaflet `Tooltip` wrapper is made transparent with border, background, padding, shadow, and arrow overrides; the child renders the visible label.

column1: Where is the visible styling for map entry tooltip labels?
column2: In the child `div` inside `features/map/components/Markers.tsx`, which supplies the white background, padding, text styling, and `rounded-xl` radius.

column1: What breaks if tooltip styling moves back to the Leaflet wrapper?
column2: The wrapper becomes visible again and reintroduces the default tooltip chrome around the custom child content.

column1: Which onboarding route can currently be selected?
column2: Only Kournesh can be selected because it is the route with available stop data; other route entries remain visible but disabled.

column1: How does onboarding communicate future bus routes?
column2: The route menu keeps future routes visible, disables them, and labels each one `Coming soon`; helper text also says that more routes are on the way.

column1: Where is the onboarding progress indicator rendered?
column2: In `features/onboarding/Onboarding.tsx`, as two adjacent progress segments: the first is complete on step one, and the second fills on step two.

column1: Why does the onboarding first step avoid hiding future routes?
column2: Keeping future routes visible signals that the app is expanding while preventing unsupported route and stop combinations from being selected today.
